site.name: Floyd Mine
overview: The Floyd Mine is a documented historic tungsten mine in Boulder County's tungsten-mining belt west of Boulder.
Federal-derived mine records identify Floyd as an underground past producer, and USGS-derived topographic indexing places the named mine at approximately 40.001653, -105.381938.

timeline.text: The Floyd Mine was developed as an underground tungsten property within the Boulder County tungsten district.
Federal mineral and topographic records retained Floyd as a named past-producing tungsten mine in Boulder County.

moreHistory: The Floyd Mine lies within the Boulder County tungsten district, a narrow mining belt that became nationally important after ferberite was recognized as tungsten ore around the turn of the twentieth century.
Mineral-record data classify Floyd as an underground past producer of tungsten, providing site-specific context beyond the mapped name alone.

The coordinate used by Remnant is a documented mine-level identification point from USGS-derived topographic feature data. It is suitable for identifying the historic mine site but is not presented as a field-surveyed surviving shaft or portal.
